title: IAM Journey Matrix — access states and evidence flows (hosted/dedicated/private)
summary: Working draft: defines a concise onboarding/role lifecycle matrix (states: requested, provisioned, verified, revoked) mapped to evidence collection points and SIEM export fields for each deployment mode (hosted, dedicated, private). Includes sample policy templates and a short operational checklist for evidence automation and weekly reviews.
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures the ‘IAM journey’ for user/service identities across Redwood deployment tiers — hosted API, Dedicated (reserved capacity), and Private (VPC/on-prem) — with the explicit goal of making evidence collection and SIEM export consistent and automatable. It is intended for secops, cloud infra, SRE, and the audit automation owners.

Scope:
- Actors: human users (console/API), service principals (deploy agents, model-serving pools), automation bots (backups, telemetry).
- Environments: hosted (Redwood multi-tenant control plane + managed infra), dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pools with Redwood-managed runtime), private (customer-managed network or on-prem bundle).
- Outcome: a small, actionable matrix that ties role lifecycle states to the minimal evidence artifacts required for an auditor and the SIEM fields we must export.

High-level model (states):
1) requested — identity has a pending access request (Jira or identity-request flow). Evidence: request ticket id, approver, justification string, TTL/expiration suggestion.
2) provisioned — credentials/role granted; infrastructure records created. Evidence: IAM grant record, policy version, issuance timestamp, issuing principal.
3) verified — periodic attestation completed (owner attested, or usage-based verification). Evidence: attestation timestamp, verifier id, attestation note (if any).
4) revoked — access removed/expired. Evidence: revoke timestamp, revoke mechanism (manual/automated/expiry), residual access check result.

Per-environment differences (short):
- Hosted:
  - Access granularity: Redwood control plane roles + token-scoped API keys.
  - Evidence sources: control-plane audit log, token creation events, route-level usage logs.
  - SIEM exports must include: request_id, token_id (hashed), customer_id, model_id (optional), route, issuing_admin, grant_policy_version, environment=hosted.
  - Revocation model: immediate token invalidation via control plane; must emit revoke event and cache-invalidation notice.

- Dedicated:
  - Access granularity: RBAC for control plane + dedicated infra role bindings (cluster-level).
  - Evidence sources: control-plane audit + dedicated cluster auth logs (e.g., kube-audit), device-level grants (GPU pool ACLs).
  - SIEM exports: include cluster_id, pool_id, node_tags, policy_hash, approver_group.
  - Revocation model: two-stage (control-plane revoke, then pool-level enforcement); ensure reconcile job logs enforcement success/failure.

- Private:
  - Access granularity: customer-managed identity backends (OIDC/SAML/AD) + Redwood agent-level bindings.
  - Evidence sources: customer-provided assertion tokens, agent attestations, local audit files (if on-prem).
  - SIEM exports: must carry correlation_id to customer audit (customer_audit_ref), azure/ad group id or saml_assertion_hash, and environment=private.
  - Revocation model: may be delayed depending on customer sync; include proof-of-sync timestamp in evidence.

Minimum evidence matrix (one-line per state, per env):
- Requested:
  - Hosted: ticket_id, requester_email, request_scope, requested_duration.
  - Dedicated: ticket_id, customer_contact, requested_pool, justification_blob.
  - Private: ticket_id, customer_oncall, requested_agent_scope, SAML assertion snapshot.
- Provisioned:
  - Hosted: grant_record_id, token_hash, grant_policy_version, issued_by.
  - Dedicated: grant_record_id, cluster_binding_id, kube_subject_hash, issued_by.
  - Private: agent_binding_id, assertion_ref, enrollment_manifest_digest, issued_by (customer or Redwood automation).
- Verified:
  - All envs: attestation_id, attestor, attestation_notes, verification_ttl.
- Revoked:
  - All envs: revoke_event_id, revoke_cause, enforcement_status, verification_after_revoke (pass/fail).

SIEM export field mapping (recommended canonical fields):
- timestamp
- event_type (iam.request | iam.grant | iam.attest | iam.revoke)
- environment (hosted|dedicated|private)
- principal_type (human|service|bot)
- principal_id (hash)
- request_id
- grant_id
- policy_version
- resource_scope (string)
- approver_id
- attestation_id
- enforcement_status
- correlation_ids (comma-separated strings if present)
- raw_evidence_reference (s3:// or gs:// or customer-sys-ref)

Operational notes for evidence automation:
- Source-of-truth for hosted & dedicated: control-plane audit stream. Build consumers that transform raw audit events into canonical SIEM fields above. Use streaming lambda/beam job that normalizes timestamp and emits a compact iam.* envelope.
- Private: require customer to supply a daily evidence bundle or enable a secure agent to push attestations. Provide a validator CLI that checks bundle checksum and emits SIEM-friendly records.
- Reconciliation: implement a weekly job (security-scheduled) that checks: active grants vs. last usage, un-attested grants older than 90 days, and failed revocation events. Store reconciliation run id as attestation evidence when owners manually review.

Sample minimal IAM policy snippets (high-level, text only — not exhaustive):
- Hosted: allow role 'console-reader' to list routes and view tokens, deny token_create unless role includes 'token-admin'.
- Dedicated: cluster-binding with minimal verbs (monitoring/read) for SRE on dedicated pools; provide separate 'pool-admin' role for capacity ops.
- Private: agent role: only signing and heartbeat; provisioning actions require customer-signed CSR and an out-of-band approval.

Checklist for onboarding a new role (short actionable):
1) Create request ticket with justification and TTL.
2) Assign initial approver (team lead or delegated approver).
3) Provision as temporary (30-day) scoped grant.
4) Auto-schedule attestation at 14 days and 60 days.
5) On successful attestations, convert to long-lived or escalate for manual review.
6) On revoke, emit revoke_event to control plane and run immediate access-validation job; log result to SIEM.

Example failure modes to watch for:
- Revocation not propagated to dedicated pool within SLA: detect and page infra-owner.
- Private sync delays: detect and mark evidence as 'pending-customer-sync' with correlation_id.
- Attestation churn: repeated attestations flipping state indicates owner confusion; recommend UX updates and clearer TTL defaults.

Next steps / action items (owners assigned inline):
- Priya Iyer: prototype the audit->SIEM transformer for hosted events (2-week spike).
- Miguel Santos: define the reconcile job's success/failure metrics and alerting (SLO doc).
- Conor Blake: draft the agent bundle validator and customer instructions for private deployments.

Open questions (to decide in the next security weekly):
- Default TTL for user console grants: 7d vs 30d? (security prefers 7d, infra argues 30d for fewer support tickets).
- How to represent cross-account delegations in SIEM without leaking PII? propose hashed ids.

Appendix: quick examples of SIEM event lines (pseudo-JSON for human review) — please note these are examples for mapping, not the exact export schema: 
- iam.grant (hosted): {timestamp:2026-02-28T14:12:30Z, event_type:iam.grant, environment:hosted, principal_type:human, principal_id:hash:0xabc, grant_id:G-20260228-91, policy_version:v2.3, resource_scope:console:token:create, approver_id:uid-32}
- iam.revoke (dedicated): {timestamp:2026-02-28T14:15:03Z, event_type:iam.revoke, environment:dedicated, cluster_id:cluster-az1, principal_type:service, principal_id:hash:0xdef, revoke_event_id:R-20260228-07, enforcement_status:success}

This is a working doc; comments inline below or push changes to the associated PR (github.com/redwood-inference/infra/PR#872). Once we converge, this will be converted into a more formal playbook with runnable transformers and policy CRs.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Prefer hashed principal ids in SIEM exports to reduce PII concerns; keep mapping table locked in vault.
- If customer insists on full fidelity for private mode, require additional contractual attestation and sandboxed log forwarder.
